question.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $t=10$ into the function. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{2})+\operatorname{log}⁡(10t) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})+\operatorname{log}⁡(10\cdot 10) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})+\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

The common logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $x=2.$ Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})+\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})=2+2=4\end{aligned}
$$
